extractions.value: This case fulfilled the proposed criteria for the clinical diagnosis of SMS, except for the acute onset of the symptoms. The initial rapid progression of rigidity and muscle spasms involving the legs and trunk led us to consider other possible entities such as progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity. However, the absence of cranial nerve involvement, the presence of normal tendon jerks, and the lack of abnormal findings in the CSF and MRI of the brain and spinal cord, along with a good response to the treatment with diazepam and baclofen, made that diagnosis unlikely.

extractions.value: Needle concentric recording. Electrical stimulation of mixed nerves and cutaneous areas of the lower extremity. The silent period obtained on a muscular spasm after a supramaximal electrical stimulation of the peroneal nerve was preserved. Motor and sensory nerve conduction were normal.
extractions.quote: Needle concentric recording.

The electrical stimulation of mixed nerves and cutaneous areas of the lower extremity induced the appearance of late motor responses following the direct evoked motor potential, showing several consistent bursts of electromyographic activity at regular intervals. This late reflex activity was also found in muscles not related to the stimulated nerve or skin area and even in muscles of the contralateral limb
